explanation: Multiply absolute decimal digits using their place values, keeping an m+n digit accumulator. Normalize each processed slot by carrying its quotient by ten to the previous slot and leaving its remainder. Strip leading zeros and apply the sign only to the first remaining digit.
timeComplexity: O(mn) for positive operand lengths m,n: each pair of digits is multiplied once, and trimming/copying costs O(m+n), which is within this bound for nonempty operands.
spaceComplexity: O(m+n) for accumulated and returned digits. Temporary trimming copies or views do not change the asymptotic bound.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: A digit pair at positions i and j contributes its product to position i+j+1 in the m+n digit result. Carrying q units to the preceding position and leaving remainder r preserves value because the original slot value equals 10q+r. Processing digit pairs from right to left includes every term of the distributive expansion exactly once and normalizes the affected lower slots before completion. Trimming zero prefixes does not change value; the product is negative exactly when one operand is negative.
walkthrough: For [-1,3] × [2,4], use magnitudes 13 and 24 with opposite signs. Start [0,0,0,0]. The pairs 3×4, 3×2, 1×4 and 1×2 successively give [0,0,1,2], [0,0,7,2], [0,1,1,2] and [0,3,1,2]. Trim the leading zero and apply the negative sign to obtain [-3,1,2], representing −312.
edgeCases: Each input is nonempty; only its first digit may be negative.
Zero is returned as [0], never as a negative or empty sequence.
Digit arrays need not fit a machine integer; do not parse the entire number into one.
The caller’s digit arrays are not modified by this implementation.
